This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s).

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1040dec12787bc121e3a7222a0d231224373f41a` — the merge of head `ba3fd25ea8aca2d5d73719fccb13e957af383772` into base `82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1040dec12787bc121e3a7222a0d231224373f41a && git checkout 1040dec12787bc121e3a7222a0d231224373f41a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 ba3fd25ea8aca2d5d73719fccb13e957af383772 && git checkout -B drift-repro 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 && git merge --no-ff ba3fd25ea8aca2d5d73719fccb13e957af383772

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b0796f023975cbdb2563e8a3ae55f6832afcb72a`
Local-runs: probe — downloaded the pinned better-auth and @better-auth/sso 1.7.12 tarballs (npm pack, scripts ignored) to read the vendor source the module headers cite; nothing built or run
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/implicit-account-linking.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-account-at-proven-domain.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/implicit-account-linking.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-oidc-refusal-cause.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-saml-refusal-landing.test.ts + read in the cited code: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-sign-in-options.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-plugin-list.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-membership-admission.ts, docs/adr/0135-identity-and-access-architecture.md (D6), content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx

### ① Derived judgments

- Implicit link through an SSO source, verification on: the accept-set narrows to an asserted address at a listed, verified domain, by equality (`refuseImplicitAccountLink`, rule 4). Right: it is the matching rule `sso.mdx` and ADR-0135 D6 already publish for creation, read through the same module.
- Sign-in through an SSO source into a linked account, verification on: an asserted address other than the account's own is admitted only at a proven domain (`refuseSsoAddressChangeOutsideProvenDomain`). Right where the sign-in would change the stored address; its reach beyond that is ④ finding 2.
- Refusal surface: no new error code. `EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED` is reused with two rule-level descriptions that name no domain; the error-code ledger and `packages/spec` are untouched. Right.
- `readSsoProviderProvenDomains` extraction: the creation rule reads the same inputs and answers the same verdicts as on `main`. Right, behaviour unchanged.
- `ImplicitLinkGateOptions.provenDomain` becomes required and `LinkingAuthContext` gains an optional `email`: both internal to the package, one caller, updated in the diff. No published type moves. Right.
- Verification off, a non-SSO source, an explicit link and a sign-in asserting the account's own address return before any provider read and before any throw. Right, and it matches the Unchanged list.
- Fail closed: an unreadable provider row refuses; an unreadable account throws, which the vendor gate answers as a refusal. Both sit behind the verification switch. Right.
- Check-runs on the head: 58 runs, 39 success, 19 skipped, none failed or pending; the two timeouts reported from the local sweep do not appear on the head.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch` with the BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset, and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required`, no stored shape changes). This is the level AGENTS.md sets for a non-protocol breaking change. The title carries `!` and the migration text names who moves. Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev open question (an address asserted at sign-in is refused even where the sign-in would not change the stored address): escalated, not closed here. See ④ finding 2. The tree and the PR's own prose agree with each other; the authority for that reach is not on any record this review can read.
- Two nearby open drafts touching the `implicit-account-linking.ts` header and another section of `sso.mdx`: textual only, no gate code. Answered, no action on this head.
- The two local battery timeouts: answered by the head's check-runs, all green.

### ④ Design judgment

Where an SSO sign-in links to an existing account, or would change a linked account's stored address, the PR makes the published proven-domain rule real on paths where it did not yet hold: the spec's own refusal applied at the remaining entries, not a capability taken away. It is breaking for deployments with verification on, and the changeset says so. Attempts to get past the guard (link and sign-in paths, SAML and OIDC, verification off, explicit link, own-address sign-in) found no way through.

1. should-fix — `docs/adr/0135-identity-and-access-architecture.md`, D6. On `main` it says accounts that already exist are not re-checked; after this PR the tree re-checks them on a link and on an asserted address. Required: a dated note on D6 recording the extension and the ruling that authorises it, as the existing D6 note records the creation rule. It is a governed path, so it lands by its own route; it must be tracked against this PR before merge.
2. should-fix — `refuseSsoAddressChangeOutsideProvenDomain`. The function judges the address a sign-in asserts whether or not that sign-in would change what the account holds. The rule as the title and changeset title state it ("changes its email address") is fully kept by refusing only a sign-in that would change the address; the wider refusal removes sign-ins that `main` and ADR-0135 D6 declare unchanged and protects no stored state. Required, one of: (a) the ruling that states the rule on the assertion is put on record (the D6 note of finding 1 is the place), and `sso.mdx` and the changeset say plainly that the sign-in is refused on the asserted address even when the stored address would stay as it is; or (b) the function judges only a sign-in that would change the address. Without (a), (b) is the reading the published spec supports.
3. nit — `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` and the changeset "Who moves" list: a link at a domain the provider does not list at all was already refused on `main` by the existing link refusal; only the listed-domain subdomain case moves. State the two cases apart. Prose only.
4. nit — tests: the address rule is pinned end to end for OIDC with the provider set to update the account; there is no end-to-end case over SAML and none for a provider that does not update the account (the case finding 2 turns on). Follow-up card.
5. nit — the comments at the SSO mount in `auth-manager-plugin-list.ts` and on `isSsoDomainVerificationEnabled` still describe the rule for creation only. Follow-up.

No must-fix. Findings 1 and 2 earn a delta review of their fix by this seat.

### ① Derived judgments

Delta review of record 6880992920 (head `b0796f0239`). Two commits answer it, then a merge of `main`; the whole net diff was re-read at the new head.

- Sign-in through an SSO source into a linked account, verification on: the accept-set is now narrowed only for a sign-in that would change the stored address (`refuseSsoAddressChangeOutsideProvenDomain`, through the new `ssoSignInWritesAddress`). Right: option (b) of round-1 finding 2, the reading the published spec supports.
- `ssoSignInWritesAddress` reads the write decision from the same inputs the vendor reads, in the same order, through the same store call and the same parse, for both OIDC and SAML; checked against the pinned vendor source. Right.
- Fail closed: a write decision that cannot be read (no plugin options, a user-resolution hook, no provider row, a failed read, a config that does not parse, an unknown method) is judged as a write, so the proven-domain rule then decides. Right.
- A sign-in that would change nothing (the account's own address, or a provider that does not update the account) returns before the proven-domain read. Right; it restores what `main` and ADR-0135 D6 declare unchanged.
- Implicit link, refusal surface, `readSsoProviderProvenDomains`, and the verification-off, non-SSO and explicit-link returns: unchanged since round 1, still right.
- `LinkingAuthContext` gains an optional `options`; `ssoSignInWritesAddress` is a new package-internal export. No published type or error code moves. Right.
- The merge of `main` brings the bare-host-name domain rule into `sso-account-at-proven-domain.ts`, `auth-manager.ts` and `sso.mdx`; none of it is this PR's diff, and the PR's hunks sit cleanly on it.
- Check-runs on the head: 53 runs, 38 success, 15 skipped, none failed or pending.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch` with the BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and the ADR-0087 `not-required` marker, unchanged. The changeset now states the rule as the tree holds it: only a sign-in that would change the stored address is judged, and the two link cases are stated apart. Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Round-1 open question (a sign-in refused on the asserted address even where nothing would change): answered by the tree; the wider refusal is gone.
- No new dev flag or open question on this head.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing now stops exactly where the published rule stops: a link, and a sign-in that would change a stored address. It makes the spec's own refusal real at those entries and takes nothing else away. Attempts to get past the guard at the new head (OIDC and SAML, a provider updating and not updating the account, a provider edited mid-sign-in, an unreadable or malformed provider, a missing plugin list) found no way through; every unreadable case lands on the refusing side.

Round-1 findings:

1. should-fix (ADR-0135 D6 note) — tracked, not yet landed. Draft #33356 carries the dated D6 note, names this PR, and states the rule as this head holds it. It lands by its own governed route with or after this PR. Nothing further is required on this head.
2. should-fix (`refuseSsoAddressChangeOutsideProvenDomain` judged every asserted address) — closed, by option (b).
3. nit (the two link cases stated apart) — closed in `sso.mdx` and the changeset, with a control test.
4. nit (no end-to-end case over SAML or for a provider that does not update the account) — closed; both exist.
5. nit (comments at the SSO mount and on `isSsoDomainVerificationEnabled`) — closed.

New on this head, nits only:

6. nit — the header of `sso-account-at-proven-domain.ts` and the comment above `validateUserInfo` in `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts` still describe the sign-in rule as "asserts an address other than the account's own"; say "would change the stored address". Comment only; follow-up or accepted deviation.
7. nit — the PR body (the 维护者速读 block and the "An address change" bullet) still states the round-1 rule and does not name #33356. Bring it in line with the changeset and name #33356 before landing, since the squash message comes from it. Prose only.
8. nit — `sso.mdx` and the changeset speak of an OIDC provider's "update setting" without saying where it is set; `register-sso-provider.ts` never turns it on. Name the setting, or say the platform's own registration leaves it off. Prose only.

No must-fix and no should-fix on this head.
